      "verbatim": "The correlation parameter, ρ Y , R , ( Fig 2 , Eq 8 ) operationalises the concept of the predictive validity (PV) of the reference variable."

      "n_counts": null,
      "verbatim": "Fig 3 shows that stringency tends to raise PPV (and lower FDR ), but setting a high decision threshold may not, in practical terms at least, rescue the performance of a classifier if the decision variable has low PV ( Fig 3L )."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "PPV",

      "compared": "classifier performance",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": null,
      "verbatim": "The proportion of progression decisions which yield true positives is the positive predictive value, or PPV ."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "PPV",
      "value": null,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "the proportion of progression decisions which yield true positives",
      "compared": "classifier performance",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": null,
      "verbatim": "The PPV of the classifier is: (10) P P V = P ( Y ≥ y t a n d R ≥ r t ) P ( Y ≥ y t )"
    },
    {
      "statistic": "PPV",
      "value": null,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "the proportion of progression decisions which yield true positives",
      "compared": "classifier performance",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": null,
      "verbatim": "PPV is an important measure of decision quality in drug R&D because the unit costs per surviving therapeutic candidate tend to rise through the R&D process [ 21 ]."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "PPV",
      "value": null,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "the proportion of progression decisions which yield true positives",
      "compared": "classifier performance",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": null,
      "verbatim": "Furthermore, PPV is equal to (1- FDR ) where FDR is the false discovery rate."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "PPV",
      "value": null,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "the proportion of progression decisions which yield true positives",
      "compared": "classifier performance",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": null,
      "verbatim": "Health authorities such as the FDA and the European Medicines Agency (EMA) are often concerned to minimise the FDR , which is equivalent to maximising PPV ."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "PPV",
      "value": null,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "the proportion of progression decisions which yield true positives",
      "compared": "classifier performance",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": null,
      "verbatim": "Fig 3 shows that stringency tends to raise PPV (and lower FDR ), but setting a high decision threshold may not, in practical terms at least, rescue the performance of a classifier if the decision variable has low PV ( Fig 3L )."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "PPV",
      "value": null,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "the proportion of progression decisions which yield true positives",
      "compared": "classifier performance",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": null,
      "verbatim": "In this case, PPV is low, even with a very high decision threshold and a very low TPR ."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "PPV",
      "value": null,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "the proportion of progression decisions which yield true positives",
      "compared": "classifier performance",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": null,
      "verbatim": "Fig 4 shows the PPV of the classifier as y t (stringency or throughput) and as ρ Y , R (predictive validity of the decision variable) vary."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "PPV",
      "value": null,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "the proportion of progression decisions which yield true positives",
      "compared": "classifier performance",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": null,
      "verbatim": "First, PPV increases as ρ Y , R , the correlation between Y and R , increases."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "PPV",
      "value": null,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "the proportion of progression decisions which yield true positives",
      "compared": "classifier performance",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": null,
      "verbatim": "Second, PPV increases if one applies very high y t thresholds (very high throughputs)."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "PPV",
      "value": null,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "the proportion of progression decisions which yield true positives",
      "compared": "classifier performance",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": null,
      "verbatim": "Third, PPV is higher when the reference threshold for positives, r t , is lower."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "PPV",
      "value": null,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "the proportion of progression decisions which yield true positives",
      "compared": "classifier performance",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": null,
      "verbatim": "The first is the strength of the effect of ρ Y , R on PPV (see orientation of the PPV contours in Fig 4 , and note both the logarithmic vertical axis and the logarithmic colour scale)."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "PPV",
      "value": null,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "the proportion of progression decisions which yield true positives",
      "compared": "classifier performance",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": null,
      "verbatim": "The second important result is the interaction between y t and ρ Y , R on PPV (see how the orientation of the contours changes in Fig 4 )."
    },
    {
      "statistic": "PPV",
      "value": null,
      "unit": "other",
      "measures": "the proportion of progression decisions which yield true positives",
      "compared": "classifier performance",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": null,
      "verbatim": "Fig 6 shows, first, that PPV increases and the number of candidates screened per TP decreases with an increase in ρ Y , R ."
    },

      "value": null,
      "unit": "other",

      "compared": "classifier performance",
      "species": [],
      "n": null,
      "n_counts": null,
      "verbatim": "Second, and less intuitively obvious perhaps, is the fact that PPV increases but the screening effort also increases as the correlation between the two decision variables, ρ Y , X , decreases."

  "what_the_study_did": "The study developed and applied a decision theoretic model to analyze factors influencing R&D decisions and outcomes, focusing on predictive validity (PV) and its impact on success rates.",
  "what_it_found": "The study found that the predictive validity (correlation between a decision variable and a reference variable) has a stronger impact on positive predictive value (PPV) than throughput, especially when predictive validity is high.",
  "key_quotes": [
    {
      "quote": "For much of the parameter space illustrated, an absolute 0.1 change in ρ Y , R , the correlation coefficient, has a larger effect on PPV than a ten-fold or 1 log 10 unit change in throughput (vertical axis).",
      "topic": "PV vs. Throughput"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Increasing throughput by several orders of magnitude has a minimal positive effect on PPV when ρ Y , R is very low. Increasing throughput has a large positive effect on PPV only when ρ Y , R is high.",
      "topic": "Interaction of Throughput and PV"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Modest gains in ρ Y , R can have very large positive effect on PPV when throughput is high.",
      "topic": "Gains in PV"
    },
    {
      "quote": "In practical terms, there is little point in investing to increase the throughput of a poor PM or the stringency of the classifier based on that PM. It makes more sense to invest to achieve high PV first.",
      "topic": "Prioritizing PV"
    },
    {
      "quote": "Furthermore, a single classifier that is highly correlated with R (e.g., the uppermost points on the lines with high correlation coefficients) often outperforms a combination of several classifiers with lower correlations with R in terms of both PPV and TPR .",
      "topic": "Single vs. Multiple Classifiers"
    },
    {
      "quote": "The use of Y may depress PPV if Y is highly correlated with X while having a low correlation with R .",
      "topic": "Correlated Predictors"
    }
  ]
